question: How should a nurse document physical assessment findings in a patient's chart?

options.A: Writing shorthand codes that only the nurse understands
options.B: Using personal opinions and general assumptions
options.C: Waiting until the end of the work week to write notes
options.D: Using clear, objective, and specific descriptive terms

explanation: Objective charting ensures that any healthcare provider reading the chart gets an exact and accurate picture of the patient's condition. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: When should a nurse perform the secondary survey on an emergency patient?

options.A: While the patient is still arriving through the ambulance door
options.B: After life threats are treated and the patient is stable
options.C: Only after the doctor has discharged the patient home
options.D: Before checking if the patient has a clear airway

explanation: ABCDE comes first! We only do a detailed head-to-toe secondary survey once immediate life threats are under control.

question: You are getting ready to give an IV dose of insulin, which is a high-alert medication. What safety step is essential?

options.A: Administer the medication without checking vitals
options.B: Perform an independent double-check with another nurse
options.C: Dilute the medication in a large IV fluid bag
options.D: Crush the medication to speed up absorption

explanation: Brilliant! High-alert meds carry a serious risk of harm if a mistake happens, so having a colleague independently verify your dose and math keeps everyone safe.

question: Which lifestyle habit should a nurse strongly advise a patient with a duodenal ulcer to stop?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes
options.B: Walking after meals
options.C: Drinking plain water
options.D: Eating cooked rice

explanation: Spot on! Smoking reduces the pancreas's ability to make protective bicarbonate and increases stomach acid, which slows down how fast an ulcer can heal.

question: A patient forgets to take their blood pressure meds and misses paying their utility bills. Which daily skill area is struggling?

options.A: Involuntary body reflexes
options.B: Gross motor developmental milestones
options.C: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs)
options.D: Basic self-care ADLs

explanation: Well done! Managing medications and paying bills require a bit more brainpower and planning, which puts them right into the IADL category.

question: Which symptom should a recovering patient at home report to their healthcare team right away?

options.A: Slow improvement in overall daily stamina
options.B: New numbness or tingling in the affected limb
options.C: Mild muscle soreness the day after exercise
options.D: Needing extra rest periods during afternoon chores

explanation: You nailed it! Numbness or tingling can mean a nerve is being squished or blood flow is blocked, so it needs a quick check.

question: How can you best support parents whose baby is in Gallows traction?

options.A: Tell them not to touch the child at all
options.B: Explain the setup and involve them in gentle, non-physical comforting
options.C: Ask them to leave the room until it's over
options.D: Teach them how to adjust the heavy weights

explanation: Parents feel helpless seeing their baby in traction. Teaching them how to talk, sing, and stroke the baby keeps that parent-child bond strong!

question: What is a crucial instruction for a patient who just had cryotherapy (freezing) for symptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Increase strenuous physical exercise to speed up pelvic blood flow
options.B: Expect complete absence of vaginal discharge for at least two months
options.C: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampon use for a specified healing period
options.D: Perform vigorous vaginal douching twice daily to clear debris

explanation: Pelvic rest is vital after cryotherapy to give the treated cervical tissue time to heal safely without introducing infection. Excellent clinical advice to remember!

question: What is a potential risk if a baby's skull undergoes excessive and very rapid moulding?

options.A: Permanent stunting of head growth after birth
options.B: Tearing of intracranial blood vessels
options.C: Complete blockage of cerebrospinal fluid pathways permanently
options.D: Premature fusion of the facial bones

explanation: While moulding is normal, if the bones shift too violently or fast, those delicate blood vessels inside can rupture. That's why monitoring labour progress is so important!

question: Which of these is a physical safety feature (engineering control) built to stop sharps injuries?

options.A: Retractable scalpel blades
options.B: Doing yearly staff performance reviews
options.C: Giving verbal warnings across the theatre table
options.D: Wearing plain cotton scrub suits

explanation: Engineering controls are physical tools or devices built right into equipment—like a retractable blade—to keep us safe from accidental cuts.

question: Which traditional practice is strictly prohibited by the VAPP Act?

options.A: Traditional naming ceremonies
options.B: Female genital mutilation
options.C: Community farming festivals
options.D: Age-grade cultural dances

explanation: That's correct! Practices like female genital mutilation (FGM) and harmful widowhood rites are explicitly outlawed by the VAPP Act.

question: What is the primary clinical use for an intravenous dose of adenosine?

options.A: Terminating paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
options.B: Thinning the blood to prevent sudden stroke events
options.C: Treating severe high blood pressure in the emergency room
options.D: Reversing a dangerous potassium overdose in the kidneys

explanation: Adenosine has a tiny half-life and is slammed fast intravenously to briefly stop AV node conduction and reset a fast rhythm. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is a major physical trigger that can push a mum into distress during labour?

options.A: High pre-pregnancy weight
options.B: Early rupture of membranes
options.C: Prolonged labour
options.D: Low maternal height

explanation: When labour goes on for too long, a mum's physical and emotional energy tanks are bound to empty out, leading straight to distress.

question: What is a common digestive problem caused by physical immobility?

options.A: Stomach ulcers
options.B: Rapid digestion
options.C: Constipation
options.D: Bowel obstruction

explanation: Reduced physical activity slows down bowel motility, making constipation a frequent challenge for immobile patients. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h4)

question: What color and look does a normal, healthy eardrum (tympanic membrane) usually have?

options.A: Pearly gray and see-through (translucent)
options.B: Bright red and solid
options.C: Dark blue with fluid inside
options.D: Yellow, thick, and full of pus

explanation: A healthy eardrum is shiny, pearly gray, and translucent, letting you peek at the middle ear structures underneath.

question: What does 'parenteral route' mean when talking about how diseases spread?

options.A: Entry through a break in the skin via needles or sharps
options.B: Inhalation of airborne droplets through the nose
options.C: Ingestion of contaminated food or drinking water
options.D: Spread through direct skin-to-skin physical contact

explanation: Think of parenteral as bypassing the skin barrier completely—usually when a contaminated needle or sharp punctures the tissue directly. Simple and clear!

question: Why must nurses and social workers check a family's home before returning a street child to them?

options.A: To ensure the home environment is safe and free from original abuse
options.B: To verify the exact square meter size of the family house
options.C: To hand the child over for compulsory military service
options.D: To collect unpaid financial debts from the parents

explanation: You're thinking like a true advocate! Sending a child right back into an abusive home will only drive them straight back onto the streets.

question: Why is a complete cure not the main goal of rehabilitation in degenerative genetic conditions?

options.A: Rehabilitation therapies only work on non-genetic illnesses
options.B: Hospitals lack the proper equipment to reverse genetic changes
options.C: Patients refuse to participate in long-term treatment programs
options.D: The conditions involve continuous, progressive breakdown of tissues

explanation: Since these conditions involve ongoing tissue breakdown, therapy is all about managing symptoms and helping patients adapt, rather than fixing the root genetic cause. Keep it up!

question: Which feature is essential when setting up adolescent-friendly health services?

options.A: Strictly morning-only operating hours
options.B: High service fees to cover facility costs
options.C: Guaranteed confidentiality and privacy
options.D: Mandatory parental presence for all visits

explanation: Correct! Teens are much more likely to visit clinics and open up when they know their private medical info is kept strictly confidential.

question: A clinic audit reveals low uptake of post-abortion contraception among discharged PAC patients. What is the best quality improvement response for the nursing team?

options.A: Discharge patients immediately without discussing family planning options
options.B: Stop offering all abortion complication treatments until rates improve
options.C: Blame patients for failing to request birth control during their emergency
options.D: Review and strengthen same-day contraceptive counseling and supply availability

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting this gap lets the team fix counseling issues and make sure supplies are ready before discharge.

question: What is the main purpose of adding family planning to safe motherhood strategies?

options.A: To ensure that families only have male children
options.B: To reduce the workload of nurses in antenatal clinics
options.C: To allow enough time for a mother's body to recover between pregnancies
options.D: To completely stop population growth in developing nations

explanation: Well done! Proper spacing via family planning prevents closely spaced pregnancies, giving the mother's body the vital time it needs to heal and stay strong.

question: Why might an adolescent with untreated depression turn to substance abuse?

options.A: To cure a bacterial infection
options.B: To improve their school grades permanently
options.C: To self-medicate and escape emotional pain
options.D: To strengthen their immune system

explanation: Teens struggling with mental health issues like depression often use drugs or alcohol as an unhealthy way to cope with overwhelming emotional distress. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h3)

question: A stroke patient is resting in bed for a long time without moving. What major leg complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Peripheral neuropathy
options.B: Arterial plaque regression
options.C: Chronic bone demineralization
options.D: Deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Spot on! When a patient cannot move well, blood pools in the lower legs, putting them at high risk for deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

question: What is the correct medical term for painful sexual intercourse often reported in endometriosis?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Dyschezia
options.D: Dyspareunia

explanation: Dyspareunia is the clinical word for pain during or after sex. It happens when pelvic lesions get bumped or stretched.

question: A nurse is discharging a patient who had a bowel obstruction from Crohn's disease. Which symptom should the nurse flag as an urgent emergency?

options.A: Feeling tired during normal daily physical activities
options.B: Mild gas and bloating after eating a small meal
options.C: Severe, unrelenting abdominal pain and persistent vomiting
options.D: A slight increase in daily bowel movement frequency

explanation: Never ignore severe, worsening pain and constant vomiting—they can signal a returning blockage or a serious bowel injury. You're becoming a great nurse!

question: What is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries after giving an injection?

options.A: Never recap used needles
options.B: Always recap needles using two hands
options.C: Bend the needle before throwing it away
options.D: Store used needles in your uniform pocket

explanation: Trying to put a cap back onto a used needle is the leading cause of accidental puncture wounds in healthcare practice. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: What special feature in modern surgical swabs helps find them easily on an X-ray?

options.A: A built-in electronic tracking chip
options.B: A bright fluorescent dye coating
options.C: A radiopaque marker strip
options.D: A magnetic metallic button

explanation: Radiopaque strips show up brightly on X-ray machines, acting like a safety net if a swab ever goes missing.

question: What is the most common minor issue that can happen after a paracentesis?

options.A: Persistent fluid leakage from the site
options.B: Sudden loss of the sense of taste
options.C: Complete failure of both kidneys
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the legs

explanation: Sometimes a little bit of fluid keeps oozing out if the tiny hole takes a little longer to seal shut.

question: How long should a patient typically hold their breath after inhaling a dose of medication from an inhaler?

options.A: Until they feel dizzy
options.B: No more than one second
options.C: Exactly one minute
options.D: About 10 seconds

explanation: Holding the breath for about 10 seconds allows the tiny medication particles time to settle deep into the lung tissue instead of being exhaled right away. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is one of the classic pillars of the school health triad?

options.A: Hospital administration
options.B: Surgical intervention
options.C: Pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.D: Health instruction

explanation: Health instruction, along with health services and healthful school living, forms the foundational triad of school health. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h2)

question: In many communities, which group faces a high risk from improperly disposed medical waste due to scavenging at dump sites?

options.A: Informal waste pickers and scavengers
options.B: Hospital administrative office managers
options.C: Licensed medical equipment vendors
options.D: Senior medical consultants and surgeons

explanation: That's right. People who sort through open municipal dumps to find reusable items often run into discarded needles and toxic waste without any protective gear.

question: Why must nurses ask patients to remove all jewelry and hair pins before an MRI test?

options.A: Metal objects can fly into the magnet or cause severe burns
options.B: The hospital requires patients to keep valuables in a safe locker
options.C: Metal items will permanently break the patient's skin
options.D: Jewelry blocks the radio waves from entering the examination room

explanation: Ferromagnetic metal objects act like dangerous projectiles in a strong magnetic field or can heat up and burn the skin. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why should you let the alcohol swab dry completely on the skin before giving an injection?

options.A: To keep the patient from feeling a cold sensation
options.B: To make sure the skin markings remain clearly visible
options.C: To let the chemical achieve maximum antimicrobial action
options.D: To prevent the needle from slipping out of place

explanation: Patience pays off! Alcohol needs a few seconds of drying time to actually kill the germs. Plus, injecting through wet alcohol stings fiercely—ouch!

question: A patient refuses a bath because the bathroom feels cold and confusing. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with personal hygiene
options.B: Cancel all future baths indefinitely to avoid upsetting the patient
options.C: Warm the room, simplify the process, and break it down into gentle steps
options.D: Force the patient into the tub immediately to maintain hygiene standards

explanation: Making the environment cozy and taking things slow helps ease fear and resistance during personal care.

question: When is it most important to routinely screen women for reproductive infections?

options.A: Whenever routine malaria testing is conducted
options.B: Only after the patient develops severe chronic pelvic pain
options.C: Strictly upon reaching forty years of age
options.D: During the first prenatal visit and for sexually active young adults

explanation: Early screening catches silent infections early, especially during pregnancy or in young adults before any lasting damage is done.

question: Which of the following diseases is closely linked to poor environmental sanitation and stagnant water around schools?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Rickets
options.C: Cataracts
options.D: Scurvy

explanation: Cholera and other waterborne or vector-borne illnesses thrive when sanitation and drainage around schools are poor. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h5)

question: What causes re-expansion pulmonary edema during chest fluid drainage?

options.A: Removing a large volume of fluid too quickly
options.B: Using a needle that is too wide for the intercostal space
options.C: Failing to give the patient local anesthetic before starting
options.D: Positioning the patient on the wrong side afterward

explanation: You've got this! Draining too much fluid too fast places sudden stress on the lung blood vessels, causing fluid to seep into the tiny air sacs.

question: A patient receives a sedative medication right before intubation and suddenly becomes very dizzy with a dangerous drop in blood pressure. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The bag-valve-mask was squeezed too hard during manual ventilation
options.B: The patient was not breathing enough oxygen before the procedure started
options.C: Many induction drugs cause blood vessels to relax and lower blood pressure
options.D: The endotracheal tube was inserted too deeply into the right mainstem bronchus

explanation: Sedatives and induction agents frequently cause vasodilation, which can drop blood pressure sharply, particularly in unstable patients. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for encouraging high fluid intake after an intravenous pyelogram?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling hungry after fasting
options.B: To help flush the contrast dye out of the kidneys quickly
options.C: To stimulate normal bowel movements following the procedure
options.D: To replace the fluid lost during the mandatory bowel preparation

explanation: Drinking plenty of fluids dilutes any remaining dye and encourages prompt urination, protecting the kidneys from potential injury. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h6)

question: When is a therapeutic thoracocentesis performed?

options.A: When trapped fluid causes severe respiratory distress
options.B: When a patient requires daily routine blood tests
options.C: When doctors need to rule out a simple skin rash
options.D: When checking the strength of the heart valves

explanation: Therapeutic drainage is done to physically remove enough fluid to relieve pressure on the lungs and ease breathing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which of these is a BAD habit when trying to stop the spread of a respiratory infection?

options.A: Coughing into the inside of your elbow
options.B: Proper disposal of used paper tissues
options.C: Frequent hand washing with soap and water
options.D: Sharing drinking cups with others

explanation: You got it! Sharing cups or spoons transfers saliva and germs straight to others, spreading the infection around.

question: A patient taking furosemide feels dizzy and lightheaded when standing up quickly. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Sudden drop in blood pressure from fluid loss
options.B: Too much potassium building up in the blood
options.C: A sudden increase in intracranial pressure
options.D: Blockage of the renal artery by the drug

explanation: When too much fluid leaves the body too fast, blood pressure can drop upon standing (orthostatic hypotension), causing that dizzy feeling.

question: How many bowel movements per week is typically used to help define constipation in pregnancy?

options.A: More than five bowel movements per week
options.B: One bowel movement every single day
options.C: A bowel movement only after every meal
options.D: Fewer than three bowel movements per week

explanation: You've got this! Constipation is generally marked by going less than three times a week. Knowing this helps you spot early signs in your antenatal patients.

question: What do we call inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, which includes the iris?

options.A: Keratitis
options.B: Conjunctivitis
options.C: Retinitis
options.D: Uveitis

explanation: You got it! Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (the middle layer). It can cause a deep, aching pain and make the eyes very sensitive to light.

question: Which factor is part of an environmental safety assessment for a client with balance problems?

options.A: Checking for loose rugs, poor lighting, and stairs
options.B: Checking the color of the paint on the bedroom walls
options.C: Counting the number of chairs in the living room
options.D: Measuring the room temperature and humidity levels

explanation: Environmental checks focus on removing physical hazards like tripping risks to prevent falls at home. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why are bedside nurses often called the primary line of defense against patient harm?

options.A: They have the legal authority to rewrite physician prescriptions
options.B: They conduct all hospital administrative audits independently
options.C: They spend the most direct time observing subtle status changes
options.D: They make the final diagnostic decisions for every admission

explanation: You got it! Because nurses are always around patients, they easily notice early changes in a patient's condition and can step in before small issues become emergencies.

question: Which condition is classically associated with a "bird-beak" tapering appearance at the bottom of the esophagus?

options.A: Zenker's diverticulum
options.B: Hiatal hernia
options.C: Gastric ulcer
options.D: Achalasia

explanation: Achalasia prevents the lower esophageal sphincter from opening properly, creating a narrow, bird-beak shape on the X-ray film as barium tries to pass. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h6)

question: How long does a seizure need to last to be called 'status epilepticus'?

options.A: Longer than five minutes
options.B: At least one full hour
options.C: More than twenty-four hours
options.D: Exactly thirty seconds

explanation: Any seizure lasting past five minutes—or happening back-to-back without waking up—is an emergency called status epilepticus. Quick thinking is vital here!

question: Why is it a major mistake to order powdered vaccines without ordering reconstitution syringes?

options.A: The powder cannot be safely mixed into a liquid solution for injection.
options.B: The nursing staff will be unable to document the doses on paper.
options.C: Patients will experience immediate allergic reactions to the dry powder.
options.D: The safety boxes will instantly melt when exposed to powdered medicine.

explanation: Powdered vaccines or medications must be diluted with a liquid using special mixing syringes before they can be drawn up and administered. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the safest site for giving an intramuscular injection to an adult?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Vastus lateralis
options.C: Deltoid
options.D: Ventrogluteal

explanation: You got it! The ventrogluteal site is clear of major nerves and blood vessels, making it the safest choice for adult IM injections.

question: What is the primary purpose of prescribing statin medications to a patient with CAD?

options.A: To stop sudden chest muscle spasms
options.B: To prevent the blood from clotting
options.C: To lower blood cholesterol levels
options.D: To increase the speed of heartbeats

explanation: Statins work in the liver to reduce the production of cholesterol, which helps slow down the growth of atherosclerotic plaques. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h6)

question: How is putting a catheter into a male patient different from a female patient?

options.A: It lacks a sphincter muscle, making insertion completely effortless
options.B: It opens directly into the abdominal cavity
options.C: It is longer and has natural curves that require careful maneuvering
options.D: It is wider, requiring much larger catheter sizes

explanation: Exactly! The male urethra is longer and travels through the prostate, so you have to gently navigate a few natural bends during the procedure.

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the rinse water flow off your arms?

options.A: From the hands down toward the elbows
options.B: Directly off the side of the wrists
options.C: From the forearms up to the palms
options.D: From the elbows up toward the fingertips

explanation: Always let water flow from clean (hands) to less clean (elbows). This prevents dirty water from running back down onto your freshly washed fingers!

question: Which vital sign must a nurse check right before giving an IV opioid?

options.A: Capillary refill
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Body temperature
options.D: Oxygen saturation only

explanation: Always check how many breaths the patient is taking per minute. Opioids can dangerously slow down breathing.

question: How do maternity support belts help reduce pregnancy-related discomfort?

options.A: They stop all uterine contractions from happening entirely.
options.B: They increase the amount of amniotic fluid inside the womb.
options.C: They cure underlying urinary tract infections automatically.
options.D: They lift the heavy abdomen to take strain off ligaments and back muscles.

explanation: Support belts distribute the weight of the growing belly more evenly, relieving the pull on the lower back and pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h4)

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: What does the important humanitarian principle of 'non-refoulement' mean?

options.A: Automatic granting of permanent citizenship in the host nation
options.B: The legal right to free higher education in the host country
options.C: Protection from being forced to return to a dangerous country
options.D: Exemption from all local taxes and immigration fees

explanation: Non-refoulement is a fancy word with a vital meaning. It simply protects refugees from being sent back to places where they face serious harm or persecution.

question: What is the primary goal when treating a patient with anaemia?

options.A: To identify and treat the underlying cause
options.B: To permanently stop all dietary iron intake
options.C: To permanently increase the white blood cell count
options.D: To lower the body temperature to resting levels

explanation: You can't just slap a band-aid on anaemia! Finding out *why* it's happening—whether it's blood loss, heavy periods, or poor nutrition—is key to fixing it.

question: How should a nurse document an adverse event in a patient's clinical chart?

options.A: Writing the details only on a personal notebook kept at home
options.B: Including personal opinions on who caused the error
options.C: Using objective, factual observations without assigning personal blame
options.D: Omitting the event entirely to protect the hospital's reputation

explanation: You got it! Clinical notes must stick purely to the facts—describing what happened and the actions taken—without finger-pointing or personal opinions.

question: What is the most reliable, go-to test used in labs to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?

options.A: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
options.B: Microscopic wet mount preparation
options.C: Nucleic acid amplification testing
options.D: Complete blood cell count analysis

explanation: That's right! Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) is super accurate at spotting the genetic material of these bacteria.

question: Which two hormones does the anterior pituitary gland release to directly stimulate the ovaries?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Prolactin and cortisol
options.D: GnRH and oxytocin

explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) are the dynamic duo released by the pituitary gland to wake up the ovaries and get things moving.

question: What do biological theories of aging primarily focus on?

options.A: Social interaction and community roles
options.B: Cellular damage and physical wear-and-tear
options.C: Retirement patterns and financial security
options.D: Emotional adjustment to loss

explanation: Biological theories look at physical changes, genetics, and cellular breakdown as the drivers of aging. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why must thiamine always be given BEFORE glucose to a deficient patient?

options.A: Glucose burns up the remaining thiamine and can worsen brain injury
options.B: Glucose stops the body from absorbing any vitamins
options.C: Thiamine stops glucose from causing an allergic reaction
options.D: Glucose mixes with the vitamin and makes it poisonous

explanation: Exactly! Giving sugar without thiamine forces starving cells to work, using up their last bits of vitamin and causing rapid brain damage.

question: Why do endocrine disorders often cause symptoms all over the body in different organs?

options.A: Endocrine glands are physically connected to every single organ in the human body
options.B: Hormones travel systemically through the bloodstream to reach many different target tissues
options.C: The liver automatically spreads hormone imbalances to the digestive tract
options.D: Hormone receptors are identical across all types of tissues and organs

explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers that travel far and wide through the bloodstream. If there's too much or too little of one, every organ that has receptors for it will feel the impact!

question: What is the main goal of giving birth control counseling during Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: To prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and subsequent unsafe abortions
options.B: To enforce government population control quotas in rural areas
options.C: To punish the patient for engaging in premarital sex
options.D: To permanently sterilize high-risk young women

explanation: PAC counseling is all about empowering women with choices so they can protect their health and avoid future unplanned pregnancies.

question: How are most common male STIs primarily passed from person to person?

options.A: Inhaling airborne droplets from a coughing carrier
options.B: Swimming in public pools with contaminated water
options.C: Direct mucous membrane contact during sexual intercourse
options.D: Sharing eating utensils with an infected person

explanation: Most STIs need skin-to-skin or mucosal contact during sex to spread. They don't jump through pool water or shared spoons!

question: A patient gets a drug that blocks opioid receptors and stops other narcotics from binding, but it only causes mild pain relief. What is this called?

options.A: Enzyme inhibitor
options.B: Pure antagonist
options.C: Full agonist
options.D: Partial agonist

explanation: It's a 'partial' player! It grabs the receptor and does a little bit of the job, but not as strongly as a full agonist would.

question: Where do T-lymphocytes go to finish their maturation?

options.A: Bone marrow
options.B: Thymus
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Lymph nodes

explanation: You got it! T-cells start in the bone marrow, but they travel to the thymus gland to learn how to tell friend from foe.

question: What is the main goal of using a steam tent for a patient?

options.A: To provide a cool environment for high fevers
options.B: To administer aerosolized systemic antibiotics
options.C: To increase total body fluid volume rapidly
options.D: To deliver warm, moist air to the respiratory tract

explanation: Great job! A steam tent traps moisture so the patient breathes in warm, humid air, which helps soothe and open up the airways.

question: What is the main functional challenge when a patient has a congenitally shortened fallopian tube?

options.A: The time window for optimal gamete interaction and transport is compressed
options.B: Progesterone production by the tubal mucosa is permanently doubled
options.C: Sperm are completely blocked from entering the peritoneal cavity
options.D: Ovulation is prevented from occurring on the affected side

explanation: A shorter tube means less time and space for the delicate timing needed between sperm meeting the egg and the egg traveling down safely.

question: Why do public health nurses and planners care about measuring disease incidence?

options.A: It provides the exact medical cure for infected patients
options.B: It shows if a disease outbreak is growing or shrinking
options.C: It replaces the need for routine vaccination programs
options.D: It calculates the total hospital building costs needed

explanation: Spot-on! Watching new cases over time helps health teams know if prevention is working or if an epidemic is spreading.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way for a visually impaired patient to tell different medicine bottles apart?

options.A: Using distinct physical shapes or textured bumps on bottle caps
options.B: Asking a trusted family member to organize and label the medications
options.C: Reading the standard small-print label by dim bedside candlelight
options.D: Placing tactile rubber bands around specific prescription containers

explanation: Trying to read tiny print in dim light is a recipe for a medication error if you have low vision! Using touch-based methods like rubber bands or textured caps is much safer.

question: Where should you place the two AED pads on an adult patient's bare chest?

options.A: Center of the chest and middle of the back
options.B: Left side of the ribs and right side of the abdomen
options.C: Both shoulders near the neck collarbones
options.D: Upper right chest and lower left ribcage

explanation: Placing one pad on the upper right and the other on the lower left lets the electrical current flow diagonally right through the heart muscle.

question: A newly intubated patient is on a ventilator. You notice the left side of the chest is barely moving and you cannot hear breath sounds there. What likely happened?

options.A: The ventilator settings have too much positive end-expiratory pressure
options.B: The tube has slipped into the right mainstem bronchus
options.C: The oxygen source has become disconnected from the machine
options.D: The patient is developing a severe tension pneumothorax

explanation: The right breathing pipe (bronchus) is a straight shot down, so tubes often slide too far in and end up ventilating only the right lung, leaving the left side quiet.

question: What does the 'Proximity Principle' mean when dealing with hazardous waste?

options.A: It should be shipped overseas to countries with large open spaces
options.B: It must be stored as far away from human populations as possible
options.C: It must be kept in temporary storage for at least ten years
options.D: It should be disposed of as close to its source as possible

explanation: You got it! Keeping travel distances short means fewer chances for accidental spills or exposure while moving dangerous materials around.

question: When wiping a bedside table in the ward, what direction should a nurse move?

options.A: From the cleanest area to the dirtiest area
options.B: Starting at the floor and moving upward
options.C: From the bottom edges up to the top center
options.D: In random circles across the entire surface

explanation: Smart nursing habit! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you aren't dragging grime and germs right back onto the spotless parts of the table.

question: Which combination of vital signs points directly to Cushing's triad?

options.A: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
options.B: High fever, hypertension, and excessive sweating
options.C: Hypotension, tachycardia, and normal breathing patterns
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, and rapid deep breathing

explanation: Cushing's triad is a late, serious sign of high brain pressure. It's the body's desperate, failing attempt to pump blood into a squeezed brain. Great clinical spot!

question: What is a major cause of faecal incontinence among women in many resource-limited settings?

options.A: Obstetric trauma during childbirth
options.B: Weakness of the upper arm muscles
options.C: Excessive daily consumption of citrus fruits
options.D: Chronic overuse of inhaled medications

explanation: Difficult deliveries with untreated or poorly repaired perineal tears are a leading cause of sphincter damage and subsequent incontinence in women. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why is it important to teach patients to finish all prescribed drops even if they feel better?

options.A: Stopping early can allow the infection to return stronger
options.B: Unused drops will expire quickly on the bathroom shelf
options.C: Leftover drops can cause severe poisoning if saved
options.D: Doctors require empty bottles brought back to the clinic

explanation: Stopping medication early before all bacteria or inflammation is cleared often causes the condition to flare up again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h9)

question: Why is an efficient food distribution system vital for community health?

options.A: It ensures steady access to affordable and nourishing food
options.B: It guarantees that all crops are grown using organic methods
options.C: It stops farmers from selling their produce in local markets
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for agricultural subsidies

explanation: When distribution works well, communities receive a consistent supply of food, which prevents shortages and protects public nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h1)

question: Why are patients with weak chest muscles at high risk for getting pneumonia?

options.A: Decreased room ventilation directly introduces bacteria into the lungs
options.B: Their immune systems completely stop producing white blood cells
options.C: Their body temperature constantly stays above normal limits
options.D: They cannot cough effectively to clear mucus from their airways

explanation: Coughing is our body's way of sweeping out trash. Without a strong cough, mucus stays stuck, and germs love to grow in it!

question: Why should you leave tubes and lines in place and document them if an autopsy is expected?

options.A: To make it easier for the mortuary worker to remove them
options.B: To prove the nurse attempted emergency resuscitation
options.C: To ensure the hospital can bill the family for the supplies
options.D: To prevent tampering with evidence or forensic findings

explanation: Spot on! Leaving them alone and documenting them keeps forensic evidence intact for investigators.

question: What is the main goal of creating a 'just culture' in the theatre workspace?

options.A: Making it safe to report mistakes openly without unfair abuse or fear
options.B: Firing any nurse who makes a small spelling error in the chart
options.C: Making sure the surgeon is the boss of every single nursing task
options.D: Throwing away all rules so everyone does as they please

explanation: A 'just culture' means we look at how the system failed rather than just blaming an individual, making it safe for everyone to speak up and learn from errors.

question: Which germ causes oral thrush, also known as oral candidiasis?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Oral thrush is a fungal infection that happens when Candida albicans grows a bit too much in the mouth.

question: Why are electrolytes important for the body?

options.A: They act as the main source of daily energy
options.B: They help run nerve signals and muscle contractions
options.C: They store extra fat inside the tissues
options.D: They prevent the body from ever losing water

explanation: Electrolytes carry electrical charges that allow nerves to fire and muscles, including the heart, to contract properly. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why are benzodiazepines generally prescribed for short-term use only during sudden, severe anxiety?

options.A: They permanently cure the underlying brain chemistry imbalance in one dose
options.B: They stop working entirely after the very first day of administration
options.C: They carry a significant risk of tolerance and physical dependence
options.D: They immediately cause severe permanent organ damage if used at all

explanation: Spot on! The body gets used to benzodiazepines very quickly, which can lead to dependence and addiction if taken for too long.

question: An unmarried young girl comes to the clinic asking about family planning, and another nurse loudly criticizes her morals. What is the best way for you to handle this?

options.A: Ignore the situation because nurse-to-nurse conflicts are discouraged
options.B: Gently intervene, take over the client's care, and provide confidential, non-judgmental education
options.C: Agree with the colleague so the young girl learns a lesson about societal expectations
options.D: Report the girl to hospital security for seeking family planning services

explanation: You've got this! Patient dignity and privacy come first. Step in warmly, protect your patient from stigma, and make sure she gets safe, supportive, and confidential care.

question: Which healthcare professional is an expert at helping a stroke patient relearn how to swallow and speak?

options.A: Clinical dietitian
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Hospital social worker

explanation: Speech-language pathologists are wonderful allies who specialize in helping patients recover their communication and safe swallowing skills after a brain injury.

question: A male patient has enlarged breast tissue during a routine check. Which body system is likely involved?

options.A: The musculoskeletal system
options.B: The urinary system
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The integumentary system

explanation: You nailed it! Gynecomastia (enlarged male breast tissue) is usually driven by hormone imbalances, which fall under the endocrine system.

question: What does the 'T' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

options.A: Tumor size and extent
options.B: Tissue toxicity
options.C: Total body weight
options.D: Treatment schedule

explanation: In the TNM system, T evaluates the size and direct extent of the primary tumor, N assesses lymph node involvement, and M checks for distant metastasis. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is a fomite in the context of infection control?

options.A: A specialized mask used for airborne disease isolation
options.B: A living insect that carries parasites to humans
options.C: An inanimate object that can transmit infectious agents
options.D: A chemical spray used to clean hospital floors

explanation: Fomites are non-living surfaces or objects like stethoscopes or tables that hold onto germs and pass them along. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: How do you figure out the true urine output for a patient who has continuous bladder irrigation running?

options.A: Measure only the dark red blood collected in the bag
options.B: Divide the total output volume by the number of hours
options.C: Add the amount of irrigation fluid to the total output
options.D: Subtract total fluid infused from total drainage output

explanation: Simple math: take everything in the drainage bag and minus the irrigation fluid you pumped in. What's left is pure urine from the kidneys!

question: A patient with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is finding it hard to conceive. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: Complete blockage of both fallopian tubes
options.B: Severe narrowing of the lower vaginal canal
options.C: Premature shedding of the uterine lining
options.D: Failure to regularly release an egg during her cycle

explanation: Exactly! PCOS often messes with ovulation, meaning eggs aren't regularly released each month. Keep up the momentum!

question: Why are community referrals and health linkages important in post-abortion care?

options.A: They replace the need for emergency treatment during complications
options.B: They ensure that the patient never has to visit a hospital again
options.C: They support long-term wellness and prevent future reproductive health issues
options.D: They are only used to track legal infractions in the community

explanation: Well done! Community linkages connect patients to ongoing check-ups, STI care, and other vital primary health resources.

question: What is the main medication given during Active Management of the Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL)?

options.A: Ergometrine alone
options.B: Calcium gluconate
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: You've got this! Oxytocin is our go-to medication because it works fast to help the womb contract safely after delivery.

question: What is the main job of the 'memory cells' created when someone gets vaccinated?

options.A: To permanently alter the person's genetic DNA structure
options.B: To destroy healthy tissue to make space for white blood cells
options.C: To slow down the immune response to prevent inflammation
options.D: To provide a rapid and strong defense upon future exposure to the germ

explanation: Exactly! Memory cells never forget a face; they spot the real germ later in life and fight it off instantly.

question: When lifting an object from the floor, how should a patient position their back?

options.A: Twisted to one side for better balance
options.B: Straight, by bending at the knees and hips
options.C: Curved forward tightly to reach the item
options.D: Arching backward as far as possible

explanation: Bending the knees and keeping the back straight protects the spinal discs from injury during lifting. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h4)

question: What happens when a germ changes its target binding site?

options.A: The drug can no longer attach to the microbe effectively
options.B: The drug becomes toxic to human liver cells
options.C: The microbe begins producing extra doses of the antibiotic
options.D: The human immune system destroys the bacterial cell wall

explanation: Drugs need to lock onto a specific part of a pathogen to work. If the microbe alters that shape, the drug just slides right past!

question: A stroke survivor struggles to button their shirt and prepare meals independently. Which therapist is best suited to address these challenges?

options.A: Medical social worker
options.B: Home health aide
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists help patients regain fine motor skills needed for activities of daily living like dressing and cooking. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h4)

question: What happens if a standard ORS packet is mixed with way too little water?

options.A: It tastes better and is easier for babies to swallow
options.B: It creates a hypertonic solution that worsens dehydration
options.C: It neutralizes stomach acid more rapidly
options.D: It becomes more effective at curing the infection

explanation: If there's too little water, the mixture becomes too salty and concentrated, actually pulling more water out of the body's tissues into the gut!

question: A clinic notices a sudden influx of new patients moving into the local community. How should this affect their commodity calculations?

options.A: The safety box requirements should be completely ignored.
options.B: The clinic should switch exclusively to glass syringes.
options.C: The waste factor percentage must be reduced to zero.
options.D: The projected target population must be increased.

explanation: An increasing population means more people will need injections, requiring an upward adjustment in commodity estimation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: Why are open-ended questions so helpful during a patient chat?

options.A: They encourage patients to share more details
options.B: They prevent the patient from crying
options.C: They shorten the length of the clinical visit
options.D: They force the patient to answer with a simple yes

explanation: Questions starting with 'How' or 'What' invite patients to open up and tell their story in their own words.

question: An alert and oriented older patient refuses a recommended medical treatment, but their adult children demand that the nurse force the treatment. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without further discussion.
options.B: Administer the treatment secretly in the patient's food.
options.C: Follow the children's wishes because they are family members.
options.D: Respect the patient's refusal because they have autonomy and capacity.

explanation: An adult with decision-making capacity has the legal and ethical right to accept or refuse treatment, regardless of family opinions. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient walks into your clinic with constant headaches, tummy pain, and worry, but tests show nothing physically wrong. What should you keep in mind?

options.A: A congenital neurological disorder
options.B: A rare tropical infectious disease
options.C: Underlying trauma or domestic abuse
options.D: Acute food poisoning from expired food

explanation: When physical wounds heal or aren't there, survivors often show stress through ongoing body pains and anxiety. Always look a bit deeper!

question: Which of these conditions is best treated with a warm compress?

options.A: An acute, newly sprained wrist with severe swelling
options.B: An active nosebleed from the nasal septum
options.C: A painful muscle spasm in the lower back
options.D: A fresh surgical incision with active oozing

explanation: Warmth helps tight, cramped muscles relax and brings fresh blood flow to soothe stiffness.

question: If a patient's skin suddenly turns pale and blotchy during cold therapy, what should you do?

options.A: Wrap a heavy blanket tightly over the pack
options.B: Remove the cold application right away
options.C: Leave it on longer to finish the therapy cycle
options.D: Apply a hotter heating pad to balance it out

explanation: Take it off immediately! Pale or mottled skin means the blood supply is getting choked off, and you need to stop the cold treatment right away.

question: What usually causes an AED to flash a 'Check Pads' error message?

options.A: The patient's heart rate is too fast for the machine to read
options.B: The rescuer is pressing the shock button at the wrong time
options.C: Loose cable connections or moisture on the patient's skin
options.D: The battery inside the computer unit is completely dead

explanation: If pads aren't sticking well or the skin is wet, the machine can't get a good connection. A quick dry and press usually fixes it!

question: When are you most likely to hook an inpatient up to a portable monitor?

options.A: During intrahospital transport to diagnostic imaging
options.B: While the patient is sleeping quietly in a stable hospital bed
options.C: During routine discharge education in the room
options.D: When filing physical paper records in the nurses' station

explanation: Whenever we roll a patient out of their room for an X-ray or scan (diagnostic imaging), we hook them up to a portable monitor to keep them safe on the journey.

question: Why do we bother grouping drugs into different classes?

options.A: To eliminate the need for nurses to check patient vital signs
options.B: To dictate the exact financial cost of each medication in the pharmacy
options.C: To ensure that every drug has exactly one trade name worldwide
options.D: To group medications with similar properties and manage vast pharmaceutical knowledge

explanation: You're right on track! There are thousands of drugs out there, and classification helps us make sense of them by grouping similar ones together.

question: Which complication is best prevented by turning an immobile patient every two hours?

options.A: Pressure ulcers
options.B: Orthostatic hypotension
options.C: Foot drop contractures
options.D: Muscle atrophy

explanation: Moving patients regularly takes the weight off bony areas, giving the skin a chance to breathe and preventing painful bedsores.

question: How should a normal optic disc appear during a fundus examination?

options.A: Sharp, well-defined borders with a creamy pink or yellowish color
options.B: An irregular white scar tissue mass blocking the blood vessels
options.C: Blurred, swollen edges with dark purple patches throughout
options.D: A completely black circle surrounded by bright green rings

explanation: A healthy optic disc has crisp, distinct margins and a distinct yellowish-pink or creamy color without swelling. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is a very common cause of esophageal strictures (narrowing) that need dilation?

options.A: Chronic acid reflux disease
options.B: Benign gastric hypersecretion
options.C: Excessive dietary fiber intake
options.D: Congenital throat widening

explanation: When stomach acid keeps splashing up into the esophagus over a long time, it irritates the tissue, causes scarring, and makes the passage narrow.

question: What is the main job of anticoagulant drugs?

options.A: Dissolve existing blood clots completely
options.B: Prevent new blood clots from forming
options.C: Stimulate rapid platelet plug production
options.D: Constrict damaged blood vessels immediately

explanation: Think of anticoagulants as a shield rather than a cleaner. They stop new clots from forming, but they don't dissolve the ones already there. You've got this!

question: Why do upper urinary tract infections need pills or injections instead of simple vaginal creams?

options.A: Systemic drugs travel through the bloodstream to reach deep renal tissues effectively
options.B: Upper urinary tract infections are always caused by bacteria rather than yeast
options.C: Oral medications have zero side effects compared to localized vaginal creams
options.D: Topical creams are completely washed away by normal urinary output instantly

explanation: Creams only treat the surface down below. For deep infections up in the kidneys, the drug has to travel through the bloodstream.

question: A rural primary health clinic lacks doctors and has very few nurses. What practical step can help improve teen health access?

options.A: Ban all adolescents from visiting the facility
options.B: Utilize task-shifting to train local health extension workers
options.C: Close the clinic until more doctors are hired from abroad
options.D: Charge extremely high fees to filter out patients

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting lets us train community health workers to deliver basic adolescent care, bridging staff gaps in rural areas.

question: What metabolic issue is closely linked to high male hormone levels in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Insulin resistance
options.B: Iron deficiency
options.C: Taking too much Vitamin C
options.D: Eating too much salt

explanation: Spot on! When the body shows insulin resistance, insulin levels rise, which triggers the ovaries to pump out extra androgens.

question: What is a major worry when identical twins share a single placenta?

options.A: Guaranteed genetic difference in blood types
options.B: Permanent failure of maternal milk production
options.C: Complete absence of amniotic fluid in both sacs
options.D: Unequal blood sharing through connected blood vessels

explanation: Well done! Shared placentas often have shared blood vessels that can cause an imbalance in blood flow between the babies—something we watch out for as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.

question: If a patient has a large left-sided tension pneumothorax, which way is the trachea likely to shift?

options.A: Tracheal deviation toward the left side
options.B: Downward displacement of the liver
options.C: Tracheal deviation toward the right side
options.D: No movement of the mediastinal structures

explanation: Think of it like a crowded room: pressure builds up on the left and pushes everything over toward the healthy right side. You're building solid emergency nursing instincts!

question: What is the best feeding practice recommended for an infant's first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding
options.B: Water and thin maize pap
options.C: Mashed family meals
options.D: Goat milk and infant formula

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, nutrients, and antibodies a baby needs for the first six months. Nothing else is required! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is a major, life-threatening danger of an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Severe chronic kidney failure within two hours
options.B: Cardiac tamponade from bleeding into the pericardial sac
options.C: Total loss of vision in both eyes
options.D: Permanent yellow discoloration of the skin

explanation: Spot on. If blood leaks from the needle hole into the tight sac around the heart, it squeezes the heart so hard it can't beat anymore.

question: Why are OR electrical outlets hooked up to emergency backup generators?

options.A: To provide power for the cleaning staff's vacuum cleaners
options.B: To lower the monthly electricity bill for the hospital
options.C: To prevent life-support and monitoring equipment from shutting down during power failures
options.D: To allow staff to charge personal mobile phones safely

explanation: You nailed it! Power failure in Nigeria or anywhere else shouldn't stop life-support monitors or surgical machines mid-operation.

question: When can a patient get pregnant again after a misoprostol medical abortion?

options.A: After six months for the uterus to heal
options.B: Never, because medical abortion causes permanent sterility
options.C: Immediately, as ovulation can resume before the next period
options.D: Only after waiting three normal menstrual cycles

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Ovulation can happen even before the very first post-abortion period arrives.

question: What is the proper way to clean the delicate lens on an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Submerge the whole device in boiling water for five minutes
options.B: Spray high-pressure air directly onto the glass
options.C: Scrub the lens firmly with a scouring pad
options.D: Wipe gently with an approved alcohol wipe following maker instructions

explanation: A gentle wipe with isopropyl alcohol cleans the lens safely without scratching the glass or frying the electronics.

question: Which factor most strongly influences whether a teenager attends routine preventive health screenings?

options.A: The personal political views of the attending pharmacist
options.B: The attitude and logistical support of their parents or guardians
options.C: The brand of soap used in the clinic examination rooms
options.D: The architectural design of the local hospital waiting room

explanation: Because minors rely on adults for transport, funding, and permission, family support is vital for accessing preventive care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h6)

question: How can long-term fatigue lead to physical deconditioning?

options.A: Fatigue triggers the rapid breakdown of calcium in the long bones.
options.B: Exhaustion forces the heart muscle to beat at twice its normal speed constantly.
options.C: Lack of energy leads to inactivity, causing muscle weakness and reduced stamina.
options.D: Continuous resting stops the digestive tract from absorbing dietary proteins.

explanation: Makes sense, right? When you're too tired to move around, your muscles don't get used. Over time, they weaken, making everyday activities feel even harder.

question: What was the primary focus of Florence Nightingale's interventions during the Crimean War?

options.A: Hospital financial management
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug development
options.C: Advanced surgical operations
options.D: Environmental sanitation and hygiene

explanation: Nightingale drastically reduced mortality by improving ventilation, cleanliness, hand hygiene, and nutrition. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why should you schedule planned rest breaks for a hospitalized patient with severe anaemia?

options.A: To lower blood pressure before giving medications
options.B: To give the digestive tract time to process iron pills
options.C: To prevent blood clots from forming in the legs
options.D: To reduce the overall oxygen demand on the body

explanation: Resting lowers the body's workload, which saves precious oxygen for a patient who tires out easily. Pacing is key in nursing care!

question: In a nursing team, who holds the legal responsibility for assessing patients and planning their care?

options.A: The most junior student nurse
options.B: The team leader who is a registered nurse
options.C: The nursing assistant on duty
options.D: The ward orderly

explanation: Spot on! Assessing patients and planning care requires professional nursing judgment, which is the core duty of the registered nurse team leader.

question: Which statement best describes a coronary artery bypass graft operation?

options.A: A healthy vessel from elsewhere in the body is used to route blood around a blockage
options.B: A laser is passed through a neck vein to burn away the plaque inside the heart
options.C: Medication is injected directly into the heart wall to dissolve old scars
options.D: An artificial plastic heart is implanted to take over the work of the damaged organ

explanation: CABG surgery creates a new path for blood to travel by sewing a grafted vessel past the blocked section of the coronary artery. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main job of the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Transmitting sensory signals from the skin
options.B: Regulating involuntary body functions
options.C: Processing conscious thought and memory
options.D: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscles

explanation: Think of the autonomic system as your body's autopilot. It takes care of internal organs and smooth muscles automatically so you don't have to consciously tell your heart to beat or your food to digest!

question: What is the main job of the blood-brain barrier when it comes to infections?

options.A: It warms the blood before it reaches delicate brain cells.
options.B: It transports white blood cells directly into the brain tissue.
options.C: It blocks most germs from entering the central nervous system.
options.D: It increases the production of cerebrospinal fluid during fevers.

explanation: Think of the blood-brain barrier as a strict security gate. It stops harmful microorganisms traveling in your blood from getting straight into your brain tissue. You've got this!

question: How should an accountable leader react when a serious clinical error happens on their ward?

options.A: Pretend the event never happened to protect the hospital's image
options.B: Hide the incident report so no one else finds out about it
options.C: Punish the entire nursing shift immediately without investigating
options.D: Use the mistake as an opportunity for systemic review and learning

explanation: Blaming people doesn't stop future errors. Accountable leaders look at the bigger picture to see what in the system failed, turning mistakes into valuable lessons.

question: Why do classic forms of haemophilia affect males much more often than females?

options.A: They are carried on the male Y chromosome.
options.B: They are inherited as X-linked recessive traits.
options.C: Males have higher baseline platelet counts than females.
options.D: Estrogen protects females from developing bleeding symptoms.

explanation: Because haemophilia is X-linked, males (who only have one X chromosome) will show the disease if that single X carries the faulty gene. Females have a backup X chromosome to protect them!

question: Why are some STIs tricky because they don't show any physical signs or symptoms?

options.A: Infected people can spread the disease without knowing they have it
options.B: Laboratory tests cannot detect pathogens if symptoms are absent
options.C: The body builds permanent immunity during the latent phase
options.D: Asymptomatic infections always resolve spontaneously without treatment

explanation: Exactly! When someone has no symptoms, they feel healthy and can unknowingly pass the infection to their partners. Good thinking!

question: Why is teaching a patient about warning signs such an important part of nursing care?

options.A: To help them cure the cyst without ever visiting a doctor again
options.B: To ensure they seek quick medical help if dangerous complications develop
options.C: To prevent them from ever experiencing menstrual cramps
options.D: To teach them how to perform minor surgical procedures at home

explanation: Patient education saves lives! When patients know what red flags look like, they can get to the hospital fast before things get out of hand.

question: Why are young women biologically more vulnerable to catching sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Faster overall blood circulation to the lower abdomen
options.B: Increased acidity of the normal vaginal flora
options.C: A higher resting body temperature in the pelvic region
options.D: The large area of mucous membrane in the reproductive tract

explanation: Think of the delicate lining inside the female reproductive tract—it has a large surface area that makes it easy for bacteria and viruses to settle in.

question: Why is FGM considered a human rights violation?

options.A: It is performed without informed consent and harms the body
options.B: It violates international trade and economic agreements
options.C: It guarantees that women will never be able to work
options.D: It is practiced exclusively in urban hospital environments

explanation: Think about it: young girls cannot give valid consent, yet they suffer permanent physical harm. That's why it's a major human rights issue. Keep pushing forward!

question: What specific condition does erythromycin eye ointment prevent in a newborn?

options.A: Congenital cataracts from viral infections
options.B: Dry eyes from forgetting to blink
options.C: Blinding eye infections from maternal sexually transmitted bugs
options.D: Blocked tear ducts from narrow passages

explanation: It's a standard protective step given right after birth to shield the baby's eyes from infections like gonorrhea or chlamydia picked up in the birth canal.

question: Why must you never leave a set-up sterile field unattended on the ward?

options.A: Because sterile drapes automatically fold up after five minutes
options.B: Because the sterile items will melt if exposed to room air
options.C: Because someone might contaminate it without your knowledge
options.D: Because hospital regulations fine nurses who walk away from trays
