options.C: The penile shaft skin
options.D: The scrotal sac

explanation: Circumcision specifically involves surgically excising the prepuce, or foreskin, that covers the glans penis. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important in high-risk pregnancy care?

options.A: Patients on bed rest have nothing else to do during the day
options.B: Mental health counseling replaces the need for medical check-ups
options.C: Chronic stress and anxiety can negatively affect both maternal and fetal well-being
options.D: It guarantees the mother will have a natural vaginal delivery

explanation: Mind and body are connected! High stress releases hormones that can impact the pregnancy, so a comforting word from you as a nurse goes a long way.

question: Which test is mostly used to confirm if a patient has fluid or consolidation in their lungs?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Electrocardiogram
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging

explanation: A simple chest X-ray is fast, easy, and gives a clear picture of cloudy areas or fluid buildup in the lungs.

question: What is a common way survivors of gender-based violence initially present in a clinic?

options.A: By demanding a police officer upon walking through the door
options.B: With vague, chronic complaints and unexplained physical symptoms
options.C: By immediately handing the nurse a written confession of abuse
options.D: With completely normal physical and mental health screenings

explanation: Fear and stigma often prevent immediate disclosure, leading survivors to seek care for headaches, body pain, or anxiety instead. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h3)

question: How does a tracheostomy differ from an endotracheal tube?

options.A: An endotracheal tube is always permanent
options.B: A tracheostomy bypasses the upper airway via the neck
options.C: A tracheostomy goes through the mouth and nose
options.D: An endotracheal tube requires no mechanical support

explanation: Endotracheal tubes enter through the mouth or nose, whereas tracheostomy tubes enter directly through a surgical neck incision. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: What is the primary indicator that the needle has successfully entered the lumen of the vein during insertion?

options.A: The surrounding skin turns pale and cold to the touch.
options.B: The patient reports a warm, soothing sensation in the hand.
options.C: A flashback of blood appears in the catheter hub chamber.
options.D: The tourniquet drops off the patient's arm automatically.

explanation: Blood entering the flash chamber confirms that the needle tip is inside the blood vessel before advancing the plastic cannula. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h5)

question: What is the most effective way for a nurse to interview a suspected victim of breast ironing?

options.A: In a busy hospital hallway in front of other visitors
options.B: By asking the mother to explain all the child's injuries
options.C: By waiting until the doctor completes a full physical exam
options.D: In a private room away from accompanying family members

explanation: Privacy is essential because accompanying relatives are often the perpetrators or supporters of the abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h6)

question: Why should you encourage families to keep talking and sharing memories with an unresponsive dying patient?

options.A: It prevents the family from feeling guilty later about leaving
options.B: Hearing is often the last sense to be lost before death occurs
options.C: It forces the family to accept the reality of the impending loss
options.D: Talking out loud keeps the room temperature elevated and stable

explanation: Even if they can't reply, patients can often still hear loved ones. Your voice is a wonderful comfort to them.

question: What is one of the main jobs of the external female reproductive structures?

options.A: Producing mature female egg cells
options.B: Releasing hormones to trigger ovulation
options.C: Nourishing the developing fetus
options.D: Protecting internal organs from infection

explanation: Spot on! The outer folds act as a natural physical barrier, keeping harmful germs away from the delicate internal reproductive tract.

question: Why do patients with leprosy often get burns or cuts on their hands and feet without realizing it?

options.A: Circulatory failure prevents blood flow to the fingers and toes.
options.B: Chronic skin dryness makes the epidermis fragile and prone to tearing.
options.C: The pathogen directly causes bones in the digits to dissolve.
options.D: Bacteria destroy sensory nerve fibers, causing local anesthesia.

explanation: You've got it! Because the bacteria damage the nerves, the skin loses its ability to feel pain or touch, making injuries easy to miss.

question: What is the main goal of community nursing surveillance when it comes to poisons and toxic substances?

options.A: To replace the need for community health education
options.B: To detect patterns or outbreaks of poisoning early
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of chemical imports
options.D: To punish factories that fail safety inspections

explanation: Spot on! Tracking poison cases helps public health teams spot trends quickly, allowing us to step in and save lives before more people get hurt.

question: Why are accidental needlestick injuries so scary for healthcare workers?

options.A: They stop the worker from ever touching medical tools again
options.B: They instantly paralyze the hand
options.C: They instantly trigger severe allergies to latex
options.D: They can push infected blood straight into the nurse's bloodstream

explanation: A hollow needle often carries leftover blood from a patient. That's why safe disposal isn't just about the patient—it protects YOU too!

question: Why is coordination so important when a hospital divides work into many specialised tasks?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any written nursing care plans
options.B: To ensure all nurses perform the exact same medical procedure
options.C: To reduce the total number of working hours per shift
options.D: To prevent fragmented care and bring individual efforts together

explanation: Exactly! When different specialists handle different pieces of patient care, coordination ties everything together so nothing falls through the cracks.

question: What is the main advantage of using secondary data in nursing research?

options.A: It saves time and resources because someone else already collected it
options.B: It gives the researcher total control over how questions are asked
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any statistical analysis
options.D: It guarantees that there will be zero errors in the dataset

explanation: Secondary data lets researchers study large topics quickly using existing records without setting up new data collection projects. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient in the emergency ward has a racing heart, high blood pressure, and extreme restlessness after taking a drug. What kind of drug is most likely behind this?

options.A: Barbiturates
options.B: Depressants
options.C: Cannabinoids
options.D: Stimulants

explanation: Spot on! Stimulants like cocaine or amphetamines rev up the nervous system, leading to high energy, fast heart rates, and agitation.

question: What is the main difference between illness and disease?

options.A: Illness is how the person feels and experiences their sickness, while disease is the medical pathology
options.B: Illness can only be diagnosed with lab tests, while disease is purely psychological
options.C: Disease is a subjective feeling, whereas illness is an objective medical label
options.D: There is no practical difference between the two terms in nursing

explanation: Illness is subjective and personal, while disease is the clinical pathology diagnosed by a doctor. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing when promoting wellness along the continuum?

options.A: Empowering patients through education, support, and holistic assessment
options.B: Directing patients to ignore lifestyle factors and rely only on drugs
options.C: Controlling all aspects of a patient's personal daily routine
options.D: Solely diagnosing medical diseases and prescribing surgical treatments

explanation: Nurses focus on helping patients understand their bodies and adopt healthy habits to move toward wellness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a simple thing a nurse can do to build trust about injection safety?

options.A: Ask the doctor to perform all medication preparations
options.B: Show the sterile needle pack to the patient before opening it
options.C: Administer all injections behind a closed privacy curtain
options.D: Hide the syringe until the procedure is completely finished

explanation: Wonderful! Showing an unopened, sterile pack instantly reassures the patient that you take their safety seriously.

question: What is the primary goal of home care for patients with chronic illnesses?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members completely
options.B: Promoting stability and preventing sudden hospital readmissions
options.C: Achieving total disease cure within one week
options.D: Stopping all routine medication use permanently

explanation: Because chronic conditions cannot be cured quickly, nursing care focuses on keeping the patient stable at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the main reason an indwelling catheter is left in place after fistula surgery?

options.A: To deliver strong liquid antibiotics directly into the kidneys
options.B: To flush out remaining blood clots from the abdominal cavity
options.C: To keep the bladder empty and prevent pressure on the repair site
options.D: To measure the patient's exact blood pressure every hour

explanation: You're right! Keeping the bladder deflated allows the newly stitched tissue to heal peacefully without stretching. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h5)

question: What does the clinical term 'undetectable viral load' mean for a patient on ART?

options.A: The immune system has stopped producing white blood cells
options.B: The virus has completely disappeared from every organ in the body
options.C: The amount of HIV in the blood is too low for standard lab tests to measure
options.D: The patient no longer needs to take their daily medications

explanation: An undetectable viral load means the medication has successfully suppressed the virus so standard blood tests cannot find it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h2)

question: When considering a vaginal birth for twins, what position must the first twin be in?

options.A: Footling presentation
options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Cephalic presentation

explanation: Great job! A head-first (cephalic) position for the first baby is usually the green light doctors look for before trying a safe vaginal delivery.

question: When handing over patients, what does the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Staff, Briefing, Assignment, Review
options.B: Safety, Behavior, Action, Response
options.C: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Analysis, Recovery
options.D: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation

explanation: You nailed it! SBAR keeps our shift handovers clear, quick, and professional so nothing important gets missed.

question: What is your very first priority when a poisoned patient arrives in the emergency unit?

options.A: Asking family members about the patient's financial history
options.B: Stabilizing vital functions using the ABCDE approach
options.C: Administering a broad-spectrum antidote immediately
options.D: Inducing vomiting to empty the stomach contents

explanation: Safety first! Always check Airway, Breathing, and Circulation (ABCDE) before trying to figure out exactly what poison was swallowed.

question: A client who was alert yesterday suddenly struggles to remember where they are and cannot focus on questions. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: A sudden change in mental status that needs immediate reporting
options.B: Normal tiredness that will go away after a long afternoon nap
options.C: A permanent personality change caused by old age
options.D: A sign that the client no longer needs any nursing care

explanation: Acute confusion or declining mental status in a neurologic client is a red flag that requires prompt investigation and reporting. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is rapid reporting of a needle-stick injury essential for a healthcare worker?

options.A: To ensure the hospital avoids paying workers compensation claims
options.B: To document who broke the medication administration protocol
options.C: To allow quick assessment and timely start of preventive medications
options.D: To replace the lost syringe in the daily inventory count

explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis works best when started very soon after the potential exposure to blood-borne viruses. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h6)

question: A patient develops cor pulmonale from chronic lung disease. What sign might you spot as a nurse?

options.A: A sudden spike in blood glucose levels
options.B: Sudden sharp chest pain and absent breath sounds
options.C: Bright red blood coming up when coughing
options.D: Swollen lower legs and distended neck veins

explanation: Spot on! Since the right side of the heart is struggling to pump forward, fluid backs up into the body, causing swollen legs and puffy neck veins.

question: Which lifestyle habit is known to negatively impact both egg and sperm quality?

options.A: Drinking plenty of water
options.B: Regular moderate walking
options.C: Smoking cigarettes
options.D: Eating green vegetables

explanation: Tobacco smoke contains toxins that damage reproductive cells and lower overall fertility in both men and women. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h3)

question: An Ebola patient is vomiting and having terrible watery diarrhea. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Stop all oral meds until diarrhea clears up
options.B: Start aggressive rehydration therapy to correct fluid and electrolyte losses
options.C: Restrict all oral fluids to give the tummy a rest
options.D: Apply warm compresses to stop belly cramps

explanation: Spot on! Replacing lost fluids quickly is lifesaving because dehydration and shock are the big dangers here.

question: Which imaging test uses contrast dye and X-rays to clearly view the inside of the uterus and fallopian tubes?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Saline infusion sonohysterography
options.C: Hysterosalpingography
options.D: Abdominal CT scan

explanation: Correct! Hysterosalpingography (HSG) combines 'hystero' (uterus), 'salpingo' (tubes), and 'graphy' (imaging) using dye to see if the tubes are open.

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to manage community medical waste?

options.A: Ensuring sharps containers are sealed before final disposal
options.B: Using puncture-resistant safety boxes for all used needles
options.C: Incinerating medical waste under controlled high temperatures
options.D: Throwing used syringes into ordinary household plastic garbage bags

explanation: Household bags easily puncture, exposing trash collectors and the public to contaminated needles. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which part of the brain—responsible for impulse control and decision-making—is the last to mature during adolescence?

options.A: Brainstem
options.B: Occipital lobe
options.C: Prefrontal cortex
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: Great job! The prefrontal cortex is still under construction during the teenage years, which explains why big decisions can sometimes feel a bit overwhelming.

question: Which layer of the skin has the highest number of specialized touch receptors?

options.A: Dermis
options.B: Stratum corneum
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Subcutaneous adipose

explanation: Great job! The dermis sits right beneath the outer layer and houses most of those complex touch and pressure receptors.

question: Which of the following best describes osteoporosis?

options.A: Rapid overgrowth of bone in the spinal column
options.B: Sudden accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
options.C: Decreased bone mass and fragile bone tissue
options.D: Severe inflammation of the synovial joint lining

explanation: Osteoporosis makes bones porous and fragile, like a honeycomb with too many holes, increasing the risk of breaks.

question: When is it appropriate for a nurse to stop performing CPR?

options.A: When trained medical help arrives and takes over care
options.B: When family members ask the team to take a break
options.C: As soon as the nurse feels physically tired and sweaty
options.D: After five minutes of continuous compressions without a pulse

explanation: CPR continues until the patient recovers, professionals take over, or clear signs of death appear. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h8)

question: Why should nurses avoid routine, scheduled suctioning of a breathing tube when the patient doesn't actually need it?

options.A: It increases the risk of accidental tube decannulation
options.B: It automatically changes the prescribed ventilator tidal volume
options.C: It can cause mucosal trauma, bleeding, and low oxygen levels
options.D: It causes the ventilator to trigger persistent low-pressure alarms

explanation: Suctioning is helpful when there's mucus, but doing it too often irritates the airway lining and robs the lungs of precious oxygen. Only suction when necessary!

question: How does knowing basic biographical data like a patient's age and gender help during a bone and joint assessment?

options.A: It helps identify risk factors associated with specific demographic groups
options.B: It measures the exact strength of the patient's muscle fibers
options.C: It proves whether the patient has an active bacterial infection
options.D: It provides a definitive diagnosis without needing further tests

explanation: Exactly! Knowing age and gender helps you anticipate certain health conditions that are more common in specific groups.

question: Why is taking folic acid very important in the early months of pregnancy?

options.A: To stop the mother from experiencing morning sickness
options.B: To prevent neural tube defects in the developing fetus
options.C: To ensure the baby is born with a dark hair color
options.D: To lower the mother's blood pressure immediately

explanation: Correct! Folic acid helps the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly in the early weeks, preventing serious birth defects.

question: Which of these describes a normal (eutocic) labour?

options.A: Surgical induction with a breech presentation at 35 weeks
options.B: Prolonged stages requiring vacuum extraction
options.C: Preterm delivery with multiple interventions
options.D: Spontaneous onset with a cephalic presentation at term

explanation: Spot on! For labour to be truly normal, it should start on its own between 37-42 weeks, and the baby's head (cephalic) should come first.

question: A patient asks how Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) works. How should you explain it?

options.A: It builds a chemical defense in your body so the virus cannot establish an infection if you are exposed
options.B: It permanently boosts your natural red blood cell count to fight off germs
options.C: It numbs nerve endings so you no longer feel any pain during intercourse
options.D: It cures any existing HIV infection within the first week of daily dosing

explanation: You got it! PrEP gives the body a protective chemical shield so the virus can't take hold if exposure happens.

question: Why do nurses check the skin right around a wound (the periwound area), not just the wound itself?

options.A: It determines how much protein the patient needs in their diet.
options.B: It dictates the exact brand of dressing the doctor must prescribe.
options.C: It shows if drainage or moisture is damaging the healthy skin around the wound.
options.D: It helps calculate the exact surface area in square centimeters.

explanation: Spotting issues early around the wound helps you catch irritation or moisture damage before the wound starts getting bigger. You've got this!

question: What direction should you teach a new mother to clean her perineal area?

options.A: In a circular scrubbing motion
options.B: From front to back
options.C: From back to front
options.D: From side to side

explanation: Always front to back! This simple habit stops germs from the anal area from spreading to the healing vaginal and urinary openings.

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to good communication between hospital departments?

options.A: Use of specialized professional jargon
options.B: Physical distance between separate hospital units
options.C: Universal and open departmental transparency
options.D: Rigid hierarchy and power dynamics

explanation: Exactly! Transparency actually builds trust and helps communication flow. Things like heavy jargon, long distances, and strict hierarchies are the real roadblocks.
